verifyByViolation.method: Two genuinely overlapping gcloud builds submit --async runs of cloudbuild.p2-juris.yaml against the live hauska-prod-497015 project, launched back-to-back with no wait between them.
verifyByViolation.result: Both builds ran genuinely overlapping (submitted seconds apart, both completed SUCCESS). Each build's own log shows it tagged, pushed, described, and pinned its OWN unique tag to its OWN digest -- confirmed by reading each build's raw log directly (gcloud builds log <id>), not inferred from success status alone. No FATAL message fired in either log, confirming the new shape-check regex matches real production output. The deployed factory-p2-juris job was confirmed live-pinned to a real, well-formed digest (sha256:d8c730b5..., build A's) post-verification -- coherent end state, no malformed or mixed reference.
verifyByViolation.conclusion: The shared-tag race is structurally eliminated: two concurrent submissions of the identical file can no longer share a tag, by construction, regardless of timing.

worktreeCorrection.what: Created the initial clone at P:/tmp/hauska-factory-build-tags (hyphenated) and branch feat/parcel-build-tags (matching the queue claim's own naming), both of which diverged from the seat registry's actual entry (P:/tmp/hauska-factory-buildtags, branch feat/build-tags -- registered ahead of creation by the planner under a different naming convention than the queue claim used). The seat-worktree-gate hook correctly refused the commit twice (once for the path mismatch, once for the branch mismatch after the path was fixed). Both refusals were honored directly: renamed the directory (git does not care about a plain clone's directory name) and renamed the local branch (git branch -m) to match the registry exactly, rather than working around the gate. No git history or state was lost in either correction.
